indication: [AGE]-year-old [GENDER] with a history of breast cancer presenting with back pain. No neurological deficits reported. Evaluate for acute fracture or metastatic disease.
technique: ** Computed tomography was performed through the thoracolumbar spine. Axial images were acquired and reconstructed in sagittal and coronal planes.
findings:
**
The imaged thoracic and lumbar vertebrae demonstrate maintained alignment. There is no evidence of spinal canal stenosis or significant neural foraminal narrowing at any level.
Regarding the osseous structures, there is a focal loss of height and endplate depression involving the T12 vertebral body. This appears chronic in nature, characterized by well-corticated margins and an absence of acute cortical disruption or surrounding soft tissue edema, consistent with an ancient insufficiency fracture. The remaining vertebral bodies maintain normal height and morphology. No aggressive blastic or lytic lesions are identified within the visualized spine to suggest metastatic involvement.
The visualized portions of the lungs are clear, without pleural effusion. There is mild atherosclerotic calcification noted along the walls of the abdominal aorta. Additionally, small, benign-appearing hepatic cysts are noted in the right lobe of the liver. The visualized paraspinal soft tissues are unremarkable.
conclusion:
**
Ancient insufficiency fracture of the T12 vertebral body without evidence of acute instability or retropulsion into the spinal canal.
